Shape the future of lifelong learning and workforce development at UCLA Extension. UCLA Extension seeks a strategic and innovative Program Director for Humanities & Social Sciences to lead a diverse portfolio spanning Humanities, Social Sciences, Journalism, Creative & Professional Writing, Editing & Publishing, and General Education. This leadership role will drive portfolio growth, academic excellence, and market relevance by developing programs that connect humanities and social sciences disciplines to emerging workforce needs. The Director will expand pathways in areas such as communication, storytelling, ethical leadership, intercultural competence, civic engagement, critical thinking, and collaborative problem-solving through certificates, microcredentials, and professional education programs. The successful candidate will advance global learning, foster community and civic engagement, build strategic partnerships, and ensure programs remain competitive and impactful for domestic and international learners. This is a unique opportunity to shape innovative educational experiences that support career success, lifelong learning, and meaningful participation in an increasingly interconnected world. Key Highlights Lead strategy, growth, and academic quality for UCLA Extension's Humanities & Social Sciences portfolio. Develop workforce-aligned programs that translate liberal arts skills into in-demand professional competencies. Advance global learning, intercultural communication, and workforce readiness. Drive enrollment, revenue growth, and portfolio sustainability. Champion civic engagement, public dialogue, and community resilience. Build partnerships across UCLA, industry, nonprofits, public agencies, and community organizations. Lead and mentor a high-performing team. Expand access for diverse, underserved, and international learners.
Advanced analytical, problem solving, interpersonal, communication and presentation skills; Excellent oral, written communication and interpersonal skills.

Strong communication, interpersonal, and collaborative skills with an ability to relate as peer to faculty, professional associations, community leadership groups, local district, county, and state personnel. Specific strengths in building partnerships.
Knowledge and facility with computers, leading word-processing and financial management software within an electronic network office environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage budgets and projects, and deliver measurable outcomes aligned with institutional goals, including revenue, enrollment, student success, and equity targets.
Ability to set portfolio level standards for instructional quality and approve instructor pools executed by Program Managers.
